item.title: Frauen-Bundesliga: Bayern’s five-star display extends unbeaten run as Leipzig fall apart
item.description: Frauen-Bundesliga: Bayern’s five-star display extends unbeaten run as Leipzig fall apart Bayern Munich made light work of RB Leipzig to claim a 5–1 away victory in the Frauen-Bundesliga, with Klara Bühl scoring twice in a commanding performance that extended the defending champions’ unbeaten league run to 50 matches. Momoko Tanikawa opened the scoring inside eight minutes before Zenia Mertens’ own goal doubled Bayern’s advantage six minutes later. Bühl struck twice after the break, and Edna Imade added a fifth to cap another convincing afternoon for José Barcala’s side. Marleen Schimmer briefly offered Leipzig a response, but the hosts could not turn that moment into a comeback. The result was more than another three points for Bayern. It was a reminder of how quickly their quality can turn a competitive fixture into a one-sided contest. Bayern wasted little time establishing control. Tanikawa’s eighth-minute goal gave the visitors an early foothold, and Leipzig’s afternoon deteriorated further when Mertens inadvertently put the ball into her own net in the 14th minute. Two goals behind inside the opening quarter-hour, Leipzig faced the difficult task of chasing a side comfortable in possession and dangerous whenever space opened up. Bayern finished with 67 per cent of the ball, 16 shots and nine efforts on target, compared with Leipzig’s four shots on target from 13 attempts. Those numbers reflected the difference between the teams. Bayern repeatedly found ways to threaten the home defence, while Leipzig struggled to build enough sustained pressure to shift the momentum. Bühl takes charge after the break Leipzig needed an early second-half response, but instead found themselves further behind. Bühl made it 3–0 in the 55th minute, giving Bayern the breathing room to manage the contest on their terms. The Germany international then struck again in the 73rd minute, completing her brace and taking her season tally to six league goals. Her performance underlined the value of Bayern’s attacking depth. item.title: How much will Zach Charbonnet play for Seahawks in return from injury?
item.description: © Kevin Ng-Imagn Images How much will Zach Charbonnet play for Seahawks in return from injury? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Seattle Seahawks will be facing the Kansas City Chiefs this week in hopes of getting back on track after losing their last two games. The offense hasn’t been as good as advertised, and there could be many reasons for them struggling as of late. One could be their lack of a run game, but that should change soon as Zach Charbonnet is set to return this week from injury. It’s uncertain how much time he could see on the field, but Ian Rapoport of NFL Network believes that it can be a lot . “I would expect him to play; I don’t know the carry load yet. He’s back full go. They really have taken their time. They’ve used the full three weeks, so I would expect him to play and to play a lot,” Rapoport said on the Pat McAfee Show. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) "I would expect Zach Charbonnet to play and to play a lot on Sunday night" ~ @RapSheet #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/rBxBi56n1d — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) October 23, 2026 That’s good news for the Seahawks, as Charbonnet is the best back they have on the roster as of now. Since he’s been injured this season, they’ve been going with a committee at the position, and though there were flashes, the consistency just hasn’t been there. The hope is that Charbonnet can give them the boost that they need, and that can even open up things for Sam Darnold in the passing game. Darnold hasn’t played like the quarterback he was last season, but the Seahawks are ready to give up on him. They’ve faced some of the toughest defenses over the last few weeks, such as the Denver Broncos and San Francisco 49ers, and unfortunately, things don’t get better as they’re set to face the Chiefs. Hopefully, somebody such as Charbonnet can make a difference, and the Seahawks can find a rhythm on offense that can help them along the season. item.title: How one pitch type could decide Brewers' World Series fate vs. Rays
item.description: How one pitch type could decide Brewers' World Series fate vs. Rays originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Milwaukee Brewers are viewed as the World Series favorites, as they have home field advantage over the Tampa Bay Rays , and also are coming off sweeping the defending champions. However, winning the World Series is going to be difficult, as the Rays are a very good team deserving of this spot in the series. A lot of different factors will be at play during this series, but there's one specific pitch type that could play a huge role. ESPN's Jeff Passan highlighted how the changeup could play an instrumental role in the Brewers vs. Rays World Series. With the Rays' pitchers' reliance on the pitch, and the Brewers' success against changeups, if that trend continues, they could be in great shape. How a changeup can dramatically impact Brewers vs. Rays World Series "The Rays are changeup specialists, and the Brewers will be at their best if they can hit them better than Tampa Bay's other opponents," Passan writes. "One thing that bodes well for Milwaukee: It had the lowest chase rate on out-of-zone changeups in the big leagues." This Rays' pitching staff utilizes changeups often, and Passan revealed that only 41% of those changeups actually were in the strike zone. With this Rays team utilizing the pitch often, it's going to be important for the Brewers to lay off the out-of-zone changeup. Jackson Chourio, William Contreras, and the rest of the Brewers' offense will have to stay disciplined and not let the big moments get to them in this World Series matchup. MORE : Dodgers facing tricky question over Shohei Ohtani's future as a two-way player If they stay patient and lay off those changeups for balls, then they could take care of one of the Rays' biggest strengths that's helped them make it this far in the first place. This might sound like a simple hurdle for the Brewers to clear, but considering teams like the New York Yankees and Cleveland Guardians couldn't pull it off, this one pitch could change the course of this 2026 World Series. There is a lot more that will go into this World Series than how the Brewers react to the Rays' changeup use. But, as Passan outlined, this one pitch will play a real role in this series, more so than one pitch might normally impact things in a series. item.title: Lions coach gets upset and walks off after reacting to star saying he’s fine not playing for team next year
item.description: Credit: REuters Images Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta ruffled some feathers across the Lions fan base when he said that he’d be fine playing for a new team next season after not agreeing to an extension with the franchise. “It’s disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt. Like last year, whatever it was, Week 9, Week 10, I break my f*cking back for this team. And then I’m going out there this year, and I’m ballin’, and maybe they’re just not showing the love,” LaPorta said during an appearance on Pardon My Take. “So I’m going to continue to do my thing and ball out, and in three months if I don’t get to wear the Honolulu Blue and play for the Lions anymore, it’s going to be all good. item.title: Red Sox make coaching change for 2027 season
item.description: The Boston Red Sox are making more changes to their coaching staff after a turbulent 2026 season. The organization is moving two interim coaches into new roles for 2027, creating openings on manager Chad Tracy’s major-league staff. MORE: Red Sox pitcher Sonny Gray reveals decision on rumored retirement MassLive’s Chris Cotillo reported the changes . Third-base coach Chad Epperson will become manager of the Triple-A Worcester Red Sox, while first-base coach Pablo Cabrera will return to his previous position as the organization’s minor-league defensive coordinator. The moves give both coaches new opportunities to support Boston’s player-development system. However, they also leave the Red Sox searching for replacements at first and third base ahead of spring training. Red Sox Continue Coaching Overhaul After 2026 Season Coaching staff changes happening for Red Sox: Interim third base coach Chad Epperson is leaving the big league staff to manage Triple A Worcester in 2027, per multiple sources. — Chris Cotillo (@ChrisCotillo) October 21, 2026 Epperson joined Boston’s major-league staff after the organization dismissed Alex Cora and several coaches in April. Before his promotion, he managed the Double-A Portland Sea Dogs, making his return to the minor leagues a move back into a familiar environment. His appointment in Worcester also gives him responsibility for preparing prospects for the next step in their careers. The Triple-A club is the final stop for many players before they reach the majors, making the manager’s role important to Boston’s long-term plans. Cabrera will also return to a role he previously held within the organization. As minor-league defensive coordinator, he will work on defensive development across Boston’s farm system rather than serving as the major-league first-base coach. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The latest changes follow the sweeping staff shakeup that began in April. Boston dismissed Cora and several members of his coaching staff after a difficult start, then relied on internal promotions to fill the vacancies. Despite the disruption, the Red Sox recovered enough to reach the postseason. Their season ended with a loss to the New York Yankees in the American League Wild Card Series. Now, the focus shifts to building a more settled staff around Tracy. Boston has yet to announce replacements for Epperson and Cabrera, leaving two important coaching positions to fill before the 2027 campaign. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

Diogo Dalot will try to impress as the right-back, while Noussair Mazraoui looks to give a good account of himself on the other side as the left-back. Both of them will have to pick and choose their moments to join in on the attack. Matthijs de Ligt will provide cover for the defensive positions on the bench. item.description: Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Bears’ Cole Kmet officially lands on IR after suffering injury vs. Patriots appeared first on ClutchPoints . Coach Ben Johnson ’s Chicago Bears scored one of the biggest wins of the NFL season so far in Week 7 action, going into Gillette Stadium and beating the defending AFC Champion New England Patriots 30-24 on a day when tight end Cole Kmet was carted off the field. Quarterback Caleb Williams poured his heart out in support of Kmet but things took a turn for the worse a day after as news was announced. NFL insider Adam Schefter broke the news that Kmet is headed to injured reserve. He will miss a minimum of four games after suffering a serious injury to his right knee, and will likely miss far more time than that. Williams is showing himself to be a leader, hitting a franchise mark not seen since 2018 . The Bears are a young team without as much veteran influence as others in the NFC North Division, which amplifies the loss of their veteran leader at tight end. Johnson’s team has a lot of growing up to do if they hope to contend for a Super Bowl appearance, but they appear to be maturing at a rapid rate and will play for Kmet going forward. item.title: This 13-year-old amateur made the cut in India but did she make LET history?
item.description: Shooting a 3-under 69 was an impressive feat for anyone in the field at the Hero Women's Indian Open on Friday, where conditions limited low scores and kept the leaderboard bunched heading into the weekend. For Ojaswini Saraswat — at 13 years, six months and 14 days old, it was a historic achievement. The Indian amateur carded the low round of the day — the third lowest of the week — to move to T-26 on the leaderboard and make the cut at DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram, an hour south of Delhi. She's the second youngest player to make the cut at an LET event, falling just shy of Ariya Jutanugarn's record mark at the 2008 Finnair Masters. The Indian amateur fired the joint best round of the day with a 69 (-3), which included seven birdies to climb up the leaderboard and make the cut. “I feel great actually,” said Saraswat in a post-round interview. “After yesterday’s round, I just wanted to play good today because I got to know what mistakes I made. I had a lot of support from my parents and my brother and my caddie, and of course my sponsors. Playing this tournament made me really excited because last year I watched this tournament." HISTORY MADE IN DELHI! At 13 years, six months and 14 days old, Ojaswini Saraswat becomes the second youngest player to make the cut at an LET event after firing a second round 69 (-3) Only Major winner Ariya Jutanugarn made the weekend at a younger age when she competed at… pic.twitter.com/VGpfwIfB0G — Ladies European Tour (@LETgolf) October 23, 2026 Saraswat made seven birdies on Friday after posting just one during her opening round 79. “I just wanted to make some birdies because it was really important to do that," she said. "I knew the cut would be around there, and I played yesterday seven-over yesterday, so I just wanted to make up for that score. I knew that I made all the mistakes yesterday." She told reporters she grew up playing at the Mohali Golf Range that was located "in front of my house." "I thought, 'Let’s give it a try,.' I was really fascinated by trophies," she recalled. At 4 over through 36 holes, Saraswat sits 10 shots off Chiara Tamburlini's lead at 6 under. "Playing at DLF is one of my biggest dreams," Saraswat said. "I have a really good support system, and my school is really good with academics, so I get to play a lot more." Aaron Rai and Ojaswini Saraswat Neville Hopwood / LET After the round, she posed for a picture with reigning PGA Championship winner Aaron Rai. The 31-year-old major champ is on an extended visit in India, where his wife, Gaurika Bishnoi, is from. He finished T-20 at the DP World Tour event in New Delhi last week.

item.title: Browns Get Good News on Injured Star Before Week 7
item.description: Quincy Williams #5 of the Cleveland Browns Getty There was a bit of a scare on Thursday in Berea, where the Cleveland Browns were practicing. Linebacker Quincy Williams, who had been among the defense’s best players over the past three weeks, was not on the practice field and was listed as out of practice with a neck injury. It was not an injury that had cropped up before and defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg offered no explanation of what might be going on with Williams. When he was asked, Rutenberg said, “I’m going to leave all that to Monk (Todd Monken), obviously, so I’ll just leave it at that.” Monken was not addressing the media on Thursday, so there was no further explanation about what was going on with Williams. But then came Friday’s practice, and a sigh of relief: Williams was back on the practice field for the Browns and presumably will be good to go on Sunday in Tennessee. Quincy Williams Among NFL’s Top Linebackers Generally speaking, things are trending in the right direction for the team on the injury front, especially on the defensive side of the ball. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger has been fighting through his ankle injury and defensive tackle Mason Graham has been back at practice since last Friday. Both are looking as though they will play–Schwesinger has not missed a game this year, and Graham has been out the past two weeks with a sprained MCL in his knee. Now, the problem with Williams appears to have been dodged. Williams, brought in as a free agent this offseason to play alongside Schwesinger at linebacker, had a slow start to the season but now, he and Schwesinger have emerged as one of the best linebacker duos in the league. Williams has 40 tackles thus far this season, and is leading the NFL with three forced fumbles, all of which came against his old team, the Jets . He also has a sack and three quarterback hits this season, two of which came last week against the Ravens . Pro Football Focus rates him as the No. 5 linebacker in the NFL, and Schwesinger as No. 18 out of 75. The Chiefs are the only other team in the AFC with two linebackers rated in the Top 20. item.title: Army football at Tulsa score, live updates from Week 8
item.description: Army football coach Jeff Monken doesn't believe there's any carryover from previous meetings, so he doesn't expect there will be any hangover from the Black Knights ' last meeting with Tulsa, which hosts West Point on Friday night. But to backtrack: On Sept. 22, 2025, Army held a 25-23 lead on visiting Tulsa with under two minutes to play and the ball at midfield. Monken decided it was best to bang out one more first down to make it impossible for the Golden Hurricane to counter. But Tulsa's defense stiffened and eventually turned away Army quarterback Cale Hellums on a fourth-down carry. Tulsa was 61 yards from goal with 1:36 to play. Freshman quarterback Baylor Hayes completed one pass and running back Dominick Richardson churned out 37 yards on five runs, setting up a field goal from 27 yards and a 26-25 Tulsa victory , another one of five one-score losses suffered a year ago. Fast forward to today: Richardson has moved on, but Hayes is back as a redshirt sophomore and the fourth-rated passer in the American Conference (134.9 efficiency rating). He's completed 62% of his throws, averaging 216 yards per game. Given Army's struggles in defending the pass, this could be troublesome. Asked if there's revenge in mind, Monken dismissed the notion. "That has nothing to do with winning," Monken said. "(Tulsa is) a different team; we're a different team. It's a different year. So it's just a game that we're trying to try to do our very best to prepare and try to win. "The emotion of 'They beat u last year; we've got to get them back' ... emotion doesn't win; execution wins." It's been a back-and-forth season for both clubs. Tulsa won its first three, lost its next three and is coming off a win against Rice. Army alternated wins and losses for four weeks, then won the last two against Tulane and Florida Atlantic . In an odd twist, Army and Tulsa have met three times previous, and neither home team has produced a victory. Army won 49-7 in 2024, the team's first year in the American Conference. item.title: Yuna Aoki leads at Grand Prix France to open figure skating season
item.description: Japan's Yuna Aoki seized the lead in the women's short program at Grand Prix France, the first event of the six-event Grand Prix figure skating regular season. Aoki, who went from missing Japan's Olympic team to winning the Four Continents Championship last January, landed a triple Lutz-triple loop combination (negatively graded), double Axel and triple flip in her 76.31-point program. She leads by 3.68 over Anastasiia Gubanova of Georgia. Olympic bronze medalist Ami Nakai of Japan, the top returning skater this season from the Milan Cortina Games, is third, 5.65 points behind, after popping her opening triple Axel attempt. GRAND PRIX FRANCE: Full Results | Broadcast Schedule Sarah Everhardt, the lone American in the women's field, is ninth after falling on her opening triple Lutz. Grand Prix France continues Saturday with the men's short program, free dance, pairs' short and women's free skate, all live on Peacock . Earlier Friday, Olympic gold medalists Laurence Fournier Beaudry and Guillaume Cizeron opened their season by topping the rhythm dance at their home Grand Prix. Fournier Beaudry and Cizeron, who teamed up last year, totaled 82.56 points for their rhythm and waltz program, the world's second-best score on the young season despite a one-point time violation. They lead by 4.66 over Diana Davis and Gleb Smolkin of Georgia, who own the world's top rhythm dance and total scores this season from Trialeti Trophy, their home Challenger Series event, three weeks ago. Americans Christina Carreira and Anthony Ponomarenko are just seven hundredths of a point behind Davis and Smolkin. They are in position to return to a Grand Prix podium after placing fourth and fifth in their two starts last fall. item.title: Sampdoria snub Giampaolo and appoint D’Angelo: ‘It was easy to say yes’
item.description: Sampdoria snub Giampaolo and appoint D’Angelo: ‘It was easy to say yes’ Sampdoria have appointed Luca D’Angelo as their new coach, overlooking Marco Giampaolo after sacking Bernardo Corradi earlier this week. According to Sky Sport Italia , the 55-year-old was presented on Friday after signing a contract until June 2028. Giampaolo had been the frontrunner to return for a third spell after Corradi’s dismissal on Monday , but the club eventually opted for D’Angelo. Gazzetta dello Sport reports that Alessandro Mignani, Fabio Caserta, Fabrizio Castori and Giuseppe Iachini were also considered. “It was easy to say yes to Sampdoria, it’s a historic club and a very important step in my career,” D’Angelo said. “I think so far Sampdoria have paid for the fact that they are a club that cannot be in this division. You need players with different characteristics and great personality.” LA SPEZIA, ITALY – AUGUST 18: Simone Ghidoti reacts with disappointment during a shoot-out in the Coppa Italia match between Spezia Calcio and UC Sampdoria at Stadio Alberto Picco on August 18, 2025 in La Spezia, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images) D’Angelo inherits a Sampdoria side bottom of Serie B The former Pisa and Spezia coach takes over a team bottom of the table with four points from seven games. Supporters’ groups have also called a protest march for 31 October. He led Spezia to the Serie B play-off final in 2025 and will bring former midfielder Luca Mora with him as his assistant. Attilio Lombardo, who took training in the interim, will stay on the staff. D’Angelo believes the players are still committed. “There are lads who care about the team and about Sampdoria, because they realise where they are.” His first game is away to Südtirol on Saturday, followed by a trip to Ascoli. Sampdoria are the fourth Serie B club to change coach this season.

item.title: How massive Connor Hellebuyck deal might have impact on Red Wings, Dylan Larkin
item.description: A massive NHL trade may have ramifications for a Detroit Red Wings star. The Winnipeg Jets traded goalie Connor Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils for a package of players and picks on Friday, Oct. 23, in the biggest trade so far of the NHL season. Hellebuyck, a gold-medal winner with Team USA in the 2026 Winter Olympics, is considered by many to be the best goalie in the league. So, where do the Red Wings and Dylan Larkin fit into all of this? Larkin has had an ongoing trade request from the team since June, something the Red Wings are under no obligation to honor with Larkin under contract for the next five seasons. However, according to The Athletics' Pierre LeBrun, the Hellebuyck trade may clear up a couple of options for Larkin. Minnesota the top contender? In an article published on Friday, Oct. 23, LeBrun says that the Wild have been pursuing a deal for Larkin for months. "No team has made more trade offers to Detroit over the past few months than Minnesota, according to league sources, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss private negotiations," he wrote. Larkin and the Wild seem to have mutual interest in an acquisition, with Larkin including the Wild on his initial list of three preferred trade destinations, along with the Florida Panthers and the Vegas Golden Knights. The Winnipeg Jets traded goalie Connor Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils for a package of players and picks on Friday, Oct. 23, in the biggest trade so far of the NHL season. "No team has made more trade offers to Detroit over the past few months than Minnesota, according to league sources, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss private negotiations," he wrote. Larkin and the Wild seem to have mutual interest in an acquisition, with Larkin including the Wild on his initial list of three preferred trade destinations, along with the Florida Panthers and the Vegas Golden Knights. The Wild are also looking to upgrade their front line after finishing the 2024-25 season with 104 regular season points but bowing out in the first round of the playoffs to Vegas. Larkin may also want to join the Wild to reunite with fellow American star Jack Hughes, who won a gold medal with Larkin and Hellebuyck in Italy this winter, while the Wild may want to land Larkin to convince Hughes to sign a long-term extension in Minnesota. item.title: Fantasy Football Injury Impact: Quinshon Judkins Set To Return, While Dylan Sampson Remains Questionable
item.description: Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins (10) before the game between the Browns and the Buffalo Bills at Huntington Bank Field. Mandatory Credit: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cleveland Browns will be getting running back Quinshon Judkins back this week from his ankle injury after missing just one week. He is in line to handle a near bell-cow workload in Week 7 against the Tennessee Titans. Dylan Sampson, who looked to be ready to return, is listed as questionable for Sunday's game. We'd expect him to play, but he's not a lock. It looks like he could be trending toward being a game-time decision. Fantasy Impact RB Quinshon Judkins, Cleveland Browns This should be a big week for Judkins, in what projects to be a positive game script against the Titans. We expect him to handle a ton of volume, and he could be a full bell-cow back if Sampson ends up being inactive. With Sampson out, not only will Judkins get almost all the carries and goal-line work, but he'll also see a boost in targets in the passing attack. If Sampson does play, he would cut into his passing-down work. RB Dylan Sampson, Cleveland Browns With Judkins back, you can't start Sampson in his first game back off of injured reserve. All he can do this week is damage Judkins. We don't view him as having much standalone value at all, even as a flex option. He's far too risky to start in Week 7. RB Jaleel McLaughlin, Cleveland Browns It is safe to cut McLaughlin as well as Audric Estime. Judkins is back, and Sampson will be back soon enough that neither of them holds any value moving forward. Cast them both to the waiver wire and replace them with a more valuable fantasy asset. There is a chance that McLaughlin plays a minor role in the passing game this week if Sampson is out. Estime is completely useless with Judkins out and might not even be on the roster. Still, you aren't starting either of them regardless. item.title: NWSL drops controversial criteria around ‘Rodman Rule’ in settlement with NWSLPA
item.description: Any player will be eligible for High Impact Player status Requirements had included top 100, marketability lists Sides also resolve grievance on Rodman contract refusal The NWSL and the NWSL Players Association have reached a settlement to drop the restrictive criteria around the controversial High Impact Player (HIP) rule, allowing any player to earn the league’s highest salaries. The NWSL introduced the rule late last year, allowing teams to spend an additional $1m above the salary cap to sign star players. Players with the designation had to meet one of eight criteria, ranging from US national team minutes and Ballon d’Or recognition to NWSL Best XI honors to media lists, including the Guardian’s Top 100 and a ranking that ordered athletes by marketability. item.title: Eagles injury update doesn't bode well for DeVonta Smith for Week 7 vs. Cowboys
item.description: Eagles injury update doesn't bode well for DeVonta Smith for Week 7 vs. Cowboys originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There might not be a team in the NFL dealing with more injury issues than the Philadelphia Eagles during the 2026 NFL season through six weeks. As the team prepares for Week 7 against the Dallas Cowboys , their injury report consists of nearly half of the 53-man roster. That includes DeVonta Smith, the team's No. 1 wide receiver after the offseason A.J. Brown trade. When he's played, he's been great. Unfortunately for the Eagles, the Week 7 update for their Cowboys matchup isn't very good. According to Jeff McLane of The Inquirer, Smith's very much in question for Week 7, and he isn't the only WR questionable either. DeVonta Smith's odds to play in Week 7 aren't looking good "Sense I got as of yesterday was that DeVonta Smith and Tay Wicks were going to be down this week, but there was optimism that Dallas Goedert could go. Several days to go here," McLane shared. While this isn't a confirmation that Smith, Dallas Goedert, or Dontayvion Wicks are going to miss or play in Week 7, it certainly doesn't bode well for at least both of these WRs. Facing a bad Cowboys defense, the Eagles might be without their top two wide receivers. Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper would be next in line in this offense, with Goedert and a few other tight ends likely being involved. MORE : ESPN analyst proposes Eagles trade Saquon Barkley to Texans for very intriguing haul While the Eagles got some good news recently with Saquon Barkley returning to practice, this update on Smith and Wicks is a bad sign for their statuses for Week 7. For as bad as things have gone for the Eagles this season, if they were to rattle off a couple of wins these next couple of weeks, they could actually be in decent shape to make a playoff spot. But Tanner McKee might not have his top two WRs, and his tight end isn't a lock to play this week either. All three could end up going, but this report and their non-participation at practice are certainly worth worrying about. item.title: Nina Drama's hajib stirs controversy at UFC 333 in Saudi Arabia
item.description: Nina Drama , the UFC personality known for her lighthearted interviews and revealing outfits, created a stir in Abu Dhabi, Saudi Arabia this week when she wore a hajib. Now it might be the most famous head covering in Saudi Arabia. It was the condition of an interview with UFC fighter Movsar Evloev , a practicing Muslim from Russian. He will fight for the featherweight title against reigning champion Alexander Volkanovski Saturday, Oct. 24 in Abu Dhabi. Drama, whose legal name is Nina-Marie Daniel, indicated this was not universally applauded. "I never imagined that me showing respect and wearing a hijab to interview Movsar Evloev would be so controversial… but then again everything I do is somehow always controversial,’’ she wrote on X. Why Nina Drama was required to wear a hijab Evloev later explained he told Drama she had to wear the hijab because he thought she would refuse and then he would get out of the interview. item.title: Fueled By Halftime Message, Ivica Zubac Shows Why Pacers Traded For Him
item.description: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 21: Zion Williamson #1 of the New Orleans Pelicans shoots over Ivica Zubac #40 of the Indiana Pacers during the first quarter of an NBA game at Smoothie King Center on October 21, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Sean Gardner/Getty Images) Getty Images NEW ORLEANS – Ivica Zubac wasn’t the player he is capable of being in the first half of the Indiana Pacers season opener Wednesday night. The big man, known primarily for his rebounding, defense, and bruising screens, entered halftime with just three rebounds to his name. Through two quarters, Zubac and the Pacers were getting outworked. Their opponent, the New Orleans Pelicans, held a 30-15 edge on the glass and were scooping up most of the loose balls. Thanks in part to their unmatched effort, the Pelicans led by 10 at halftime. “The second quarter… was well below standards from a standpoint of intensity and passion to compete. Just wasn’t good,” Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle said postgame. He cited the rebounding margin as evidence of that and added that, per tracking from his assistants, the Pacers grabbed just 35% of the loose balls across the first two quarters. “That just shows that you’re not playing hard enough,” Carlisle said. “And so, [we] had a pretty animated discussion about it at halftime.” Rebounding requires a team effort. But Zubac is supposed to provide a massive boost to that operation. During the preseason, the Croatian big man had two games in which he pulled in double-digit rebounds in just one half. His power and positioning is hard to match. That’s what made his first half – with just three rebounds as New Orleans outworked Indiana – disappointing. “The way we played, especially in the second quarter, there’s no excuse for that,” Zubac said. The whole team needed to hear Carlisle’s message. But Zubac, who the Pacers traded for in part because of his elite abilities on the glass, really needed it. And he responded. What did Ivica Zubac do in the second half of the Pacers season opener? After pulling in just three boards in the first half, Zubac grabbed three after just 3:19 of third-quarter action. The Pacers scored, or drew a foul, within 11 seconds of each one – when their center gets a rebound, the Pacers love to push the pace offensively. Zubac pulled in seven rebounds in just the third quarter as the Pacers began their comeback. He nearly equaled the offensive rebounding total of the entire Pelicans team in that frame. After hearing it from his head coach at halftime, Zubac lifted his level of play. “We couldn’t rebound. We couldn’t win any loose balls. We needed that.” Zubac said of his team’s first-half play before Carlisle’s message. I’ve gotta help the guys more, just to finish the possessions so we can run,” Zubac said. “Any time we ran, we got something good out of it. We just couldn’t control the rebounds [early]. Since Carlisle became the Pacers head coach again in 2021, only 10 other players had pulled in at least 15 rebounds in one game. There were only 25 individual performances reaching that mark. But his halftime attitude and message brought out the best in his players, and in particular his new starting center. Zubac’s second-half play made the Pacers comeback possible. “Guys did a great job in the second half of being combative and fighting,” Carlisle said. “Fighting a lot harder than we did in the first half.” That fight has the Pacers at 1-0 to start their campaign. item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
